chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Ismail from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl from Abu al-Subah al-Kinanī from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

I said to him, 'What is your view of a merchant who has wealth when he delays the Hajj every year, and he is not occupied from it except by trade or debt?' So he said, 'There is no excuse for him delaying the Hajj. If he dies having left the Hajj, he has left a law from the laws of Islam.'
Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umeyr from Hammad from al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), similar to it.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a wealthy person who delays Hajj every year due to business or debt?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that worldly pursuits like trade or settling debts do not constitute a valid excuse for perpetually deferring the Hajj obligation. The Imam emphasizes that dying without performing Hajj while having the means constitutes the abandonment of a fundamental pillar of Islam, underscoring the urgency of fulfilling this duty before death. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly view that financial activity, while permissible, does not indefinitely supersede the fixed time for obligatory worship.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Ismail, form Muhammad Bin Al Fuzayl, from Abu Al Sabbah Al Kinany, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘

I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘What is your<sup>asws</sup> view of a business man with wealth when he delays the Hajj every year, and he is not pre-occupied from it except by the business, or the debts?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no excuse for him to delay the Hajj. If he were to die having had neglected the Hajj, so he would have neglected a Law from the Laws of Al-Islam’.
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, from Abu Abdullahasws, similar to it’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Isma‘il from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl from abu al-Sabbah al-Kinaniy who has said the following: “

I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘What do you say about a wealthy business man who procrastinates in performing al-Hajj every year when no other thing prevents him from al-Hajj except business and debts?’ He (the Imam) replied, ‘He does not have any good excuse. He must not procrastinate performing al-Hajj. If he dies, he has violated one of the laws of al-Islam.’”
